preconditions.description: The number of railway stations n is an integer between 2 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: The railway network is represented by exactly n-1 undirected edges, where each edge connects two distinct stations within the range 1 to n.
The number of passenger queries m is an integer between 1 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b and 1 <= g <= 10**6 for a, b, g in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query consists of departure station a, arrival station b (distinct), and minimum scenery beauty g along the shortest path between them, where g is between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.
The railway network is connected (i.e., forms a tree).

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (len(output) == n - 1 and all(1 <= f <= 10**6 for f in output))
postconditions.description: If no valid solution exists, output is '-1'. Otherwise, output is a list of n-1 integers, each between 1 and 10^6 inclusive, representing the scenery beauty values for each railway section.

postconditions.expression: stdout != '-1' implies all(consistent_path_min(edges, output, a, b) == g for a, b, g in queries)
postconditions.description: For every passenger query (a, b, g), the minimum scenery beauty along the shortest path from a to b in the output solution must equal g.
